# 1. Introduction & Executive Summary
This final report integrates our complete data pipeline—spanning data cleaning, exploratory data visualization, and predictive modeling. Using the benchmark `mtcars` dataset, our objective is to analyze vehicle characteristics, uncover underlying trends, and build a robust regression model to predict fuel efficiency (`mpg`).

# 2. Data Preparation & Cleaning (Task 1 Integration)
In this phase, we inspect the dataset for missing values, verify data types, and structure the data to ensure high analytical integrity.

```{r data-cleaning}
# Load dataset
data(mtcars)

# Check for missing values in the dataset
sum(is.na(mtcars))

# Structure of the cleaned dataset
str(mtcars)

# Summary of clean data
summary(mtcars[, c("mpg", "wt", "hp", "cyl")])
library(ggplot2)

# Scatter plot with regression line showing weight vs mpg
ggplot(mtcars, aes(x = wt, y = mpg, color = factor(cyl))) +
  geom_point(size = 3) +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = FALSE) +
  labs(title = "Fuel Efficiency vs. Vehicle Weight",
       subtitle = "Categorized by Cylinder Count",
       x = "Weight (1000 lbs)",
       y = "Miles Per Gallon (mpg)",
       color = "Cylinders") +
  theme_minimal()
# Reproducibility
set.seed(123)

# Train/Test Split
train_index <- sample(1:nrow(mtcars), 0.8 * nrow(mtcars))
train_data <- mtcars[train_index, ]
test_data <- mtcars[-train_index, ]

# Fit Multiple Linear Regression Model
model <- lm(mpg ~ wt + hp, data = train_data)
summary(model)
# Diagnostic Plots
par(mfrow = c(2, 2))
plot(model)
par(mfrow = c(1, 1))

# Evaluate RMSE on Test Data
predictions <- predict(model, newdata = test_data)
rmse <- sqrt(mean((test_data$mpg - predictions)^2))
print(paste("Test RMSE:", rmse))
